paras.t: ￼ 아래 주어진 문장이 들어갈 곳으로 적당한 곳을 고르시오.
Instead, she buys them secondhand.

《Why Fashion Needs to Be More Sustainable》 Jessi is a fashion blogger who loves unique, vibrant clothes. (①) But guess what? She does not buy new clothes. (②) You may think secondhand clothes are old fashioned, but by buying them, Jessi can try different styles. (③) She also does not get too attached to any style or brand because there is always another exciting outfit waiting to be discovered. (④) Jessi's clothing habits are not just about creating a style; they are about saving the Earth. The reason is that her actions help reduce the production and consumption of clothes. (⑤)
￼ 아래 주어진 문장 다음에 이어질 문장들의 적절한 순서를 쓰시오.
Another key to making fashion sustainable is the consumer: us.

(A) We can also reduce waste by discarding clothes responsibly. To be specific, we should buy only what we need and pass clothing on to someone who will wear it or to a thrift shop when discarding it. Circular fashion will not solve every problem in the fashion industry overnight.

(B) If we want the fashion industry to adopt more sustainable practices, we must care about how clothes come to us. We should then demonstrate our concerns through what we buy. The market, of course, will respond.

(C) However, small steps in the right direction are better than nothing. Keeping things in the supply chain for as many cycles as possible is really important. By making small changes to our clothing habits today, the fashion industry will gradually improve. After all, nothing is more fashionable than saving the planet.
￼ 아래 주어진 문장이 들어갈 곳으로 적당한 곳을 고르시오.
Today, a new form of consumer activism, known as a buycott, has emerged.

《Consumer Activism》 Consumer activism involves consumers taking actions to support or protest certain products or companies based on their ethical, environmental, or social concerns. A boycott is a form of protest in which individuals stop purchasing products from a particular company to express their objection to its practices. For example, in 2010, Greenpeace, an environmental support organization, initiated a campaign against a product of a food company, accusing the company of sourcing palm oil from companies involved in the destruction of forests. (①) In response to Greenpeace's campaign and growing public pressure, the company agreed to cease sourcing palm oil from companies linked with the destruction of forests and commit to using sustainable palm oil by 2015. (②) In a buycott, consumers actively support companies in accord with their values by consciously buying their products. (③) In 2020, an ice cream brand gained attention for its support of climate action. Consumers who shared this value actively purchased the ice cream, enhancing its reputation and sales. (④) This inspired other brands to consider their social and environmental responsibilities. In this way, consumer activism empowers individuals to use their purchasing power and voices to promote positive change and hold businesses accountable for their actions. (⑤)
￼ 아래 주어진 문장이 들어갈 곳으로 적당한 곳을 고르시오.
Material extraction, textile manufacturing, the supply chain, design, sales, marketing, and other steps are guided by the aim of maximizing garment consumption without considering other issues.

Worth over $3 trillion and making up 2% of the world's GDP, the fashion industry today has an almost entirely linear approach. (①) The process moves in a straight line from design to consumption to disposal. (②) Due to linear fashion, the fashion industry negatively affects the environment. (③) 85% of textiles go into landfills, only 1% of the material is recycled, at least 500,000 tons of microfibers end up in the ocean (equal to 50 billion plastic bottles), and 93 billion cubic meters of water is required for textile production annually. (④) Alarming numbers like these will keep increasing if producers maintain the old system. It is clear that waste and pollution from the fashion industry must be reduced. (⑤) Linear fashion must change, and this could happen through circular fashion.
￼ 아래 주어진 문장 다음에 이어질 문장들의 적절한 순서를 쓰시오.
Circular fashion is inspired by the principles of a circular economy and sustainable development.

(A) A circular economy is based on limiting waste, keeping resources and materials in use, and reusing them. In a circular model, we make, use, and reuse materials for as long as possible to extract their maximum value. Therefore, clothing and textiles are produced, used, and reused to minimize waste.

(B) Second, circular processes utilize chemicals and materials safe for human health and the environment. This practice protects the environment and consumer health. Third, materials are regenerated instead of being disposed of, which enables their long-term use.

(C) It is a renewable approach to reduce the fashion industry's environmental impact. Circular fashion provides numerous benefits. First, extending the lifespan of fibers significantly reduces textile waste, benefiting the environment.
￼ 아래 주어진 문장 다음에 이어질 문장들의 적절한 순서를 쓰시오.
The rise of circular fashion is facilitated by new technology and ideas.

(A) One company uses nanotechnology to make soft material from orange peels. Another makes fabrics from kapok tree seeds. The trees grow well in poor soil without needing much water. These new fabrics produce less waste, last a long time, and break down easily.

(B) Materials commonly used in clothing are not eco-friendly because they require considerable resources and often break down slowly. This creates a need for eco-friendly textile alternatives. Currently, companies are developing recycled fibers and fibers extracted from agricultural waste products like leaves, peels, and seeds.

(C) In addition to these manufacturing techniques, technology will improve in such a way that it may become normal to produce clothes only when people order them. This "make-to-order" method will cost more, but then less money will be spent on maintaining offline stores. And 3D technology will enable people to see how clothes will fit online without trying them on in a store. In the long run, innovation in production and sales will facilitate sustainable fashion and considerably reduce material waste and logistics emissions.

He did this to make people think The Shed was a special restaurant.

《Fake or Fact, That Is the Question》 (①) British writer Oobah Butler wanted to experiment with how easily one can manipulate public opinion online. (②) He created a fake restaurant called The Shed at Dulwich. (③) Butler set up an account for his "restaurant" on a popular online review site. (④) He did not provide an exact address and wrote it was reservations only. (⑤)
￼ 아래 주어진 문장 다음에 이어질 문장들의 적절한 순서를 쓰시오.
You should then check the credibility of the content creator.

(A) Finally, check who else is reporting the story. If no other media are reporting the same story, the story may not be true. Pick a few keywords from the story and put them in a search site to see if other media are supporting the story.

(B) If a story has no writer's name, this could be a sign that its content is questionable. If there is a name, find out what and where the person has reported before. If the person has not written anything else or writes for a website that looks unreliable, think twice before believing the content.

(C) Sorting through the vast amount of information created and shared online is challenging. However, it is important that we know what false information is and how it spreads. The better we recognize false information, the better we will be at avoiding it and helping others do the same.
￼ 아래 주어진 문장 다음에 이어질 문장들의 적절한 순서를 쓰시오.
《Digital Footprints: Mind Your Privacy》

(A) □ Posting and commenting on social media □ Sending and receiving e-mail Your digital footprints from these activities may remain permanent. Even if you request a website or social media platform to remove your personal information, someone might have already collected your information with bad intent. Additionally, your negative online activity can potentially harm your reputation or career. It is important to manage and reduce your digital footprints.

(B) Review the following activities and mark the ones that you do not participate in. Your answer should be "NONE." □ Creating online accounts □ Searching and visiting websites □ Downloading and using apps □ Making online purchases

(C) Walking on the beach, you do not need to worry about footprints. They vanish with the waves. However, a "digital footprint" the data trail left when you sign up, access, or send content not only proves challenging to remove but enables tracking of your behavior, preferences, and opinions. There are two types of digital footprints. Active footprints, like social media posts, are intentionally created data, while passive footprints, such as website cookies and mobile phone activity, occur without your direct involvement. Let's explore actions that create digital footprints.
￼ 아래 주어진 문장이 들어갈 곳으로 적당한 곳을 고르시오.
He then asked his friends to write favorable fake reviews on the review site.

He faked photos of The Shed's food with shaving cream, whitening tablets, and even his own foot. (①) Things quickly got, in Butler's words, "a little out of hand." (②) From the lowest of the charts of the review site, The Shed continuously climbed the London rankings. He started getting e-mails and phone calls requesting reservations. (③) Interest further increased when he told callers The Shed was "fully booked for the next six weeks." (④) Even funnier, food suppliers started guessing The Shed's address and sent him free samples, and many job applications came in. These things happened without Butler serving a single meal. The Shed eventually became London's number-one restaurant on one of the most trusted restaurant review sites. (⑤) According to Butler, The Shed held that ranking for two weeks.
￼ 아래 주어진 문장 다음에 이어질 문장들의 적절한 순서를 쓰시오.
Butler's story shows that much of what we see on the Internet cannot be trusted.

(A) False information is any information that misinforms or deceives people. It can be about anything such as health, the environment, and economics across many platforms. It can be influential, as The Shed incident shows. If people had been digitally literate, they would not have been fooled by The Shed experiment so easily.

(B) Digitally literate people would have carefully considered information about The Shed without being distracted by other people's reactions. They would have been suspicious that the restaurant did not have an address. They would have wondered why reviews on the restaurant did not appear in other more credible media. If they had done these things, they would likely have suspected that something was not right.

(C) This emphasizes the importance of digital literacy. Digital literacy is about more than just using computers. It is the ability to use digital technology to find, evaluate, create, and communicate information. To become digitally literate, we need to develop an attitude and knowledge that enable us to detect false information online.
￼ 아래 주어진 문장 다음에 이어질 문장들의 적절한 순서를 쓰시오.
Fortunately, The Shed incident was an experiment that caused little damage.
